measurement: 理 10866 (b) — the CANON reference, reported separately from the training split

two_references.TRAINING SPLIT: regurgitation — reproducing text we fine-tuned on
two_references.CANON: borrowing — reproducing famous verse it knew before we touched it

findings: THE TWO REFERENCES CATCH DISJOINT SETS. Not one poem in any arm trips both — regurgitation and borrowing are separate behaviours and a single 'copying' number would have merged them.

BORROWING IS NOT A FINE-TUNING ARTEFACT. The BASELINE borrows too. Every arm borrows at a similar low rate, including the untouched model, so borrowing is a property of the base model and not of anything we did to it.
REGURGITATION IS ENTIRELY e3's. Zero in baseline, iter60 and mixed; 8 of 34 poems at three epochs on one seed. That is the overfitting signature in a second instrument.
王安石〈元日〉 — the case that motivated the canon — IS CAUGHT, in 全宋詩, exactly as 理 predicted. So is 蘇軾's 浣溪沙 line and 王昌齡's 采蓮曲.
what_it_cannot_see: MING POETS ARE ABSENT by construction: the repo is 唐/宋/元/五代/詩經/楚辭. 唐寅's own era is not in it, so a Ming borrowing scores CLEAN here. 理's per-poem judge pass is the only canon that holds Ming and it is theirs to run.
Paraphrase and reordered couplets — whole-line keys, the same floor as the training-split check.
So CLEAN is the optimistic column in both directions.
